#!/bin/bash
#FLUX -N 1
#FLUX -n 1
#FLUX -c 16
#FLUX -t 30m
#FLUX -q general
#FLUX -J IONS_LAMMPS
#FLUX -o out.log
#FLUX -e err.log

# The following sbatch option is not supported in Flux:
# --mail-type=FAIL,BEGIN,END
# Omitting this may impact user notification workflows.

######  Module commands #####
module swap PrgEnv-intel PrgEnv-gnu
module load boost/gnu
module load gsl
module load lammps/gnu/7Aug19

######  Job commands go below this line #####
cd $FLUX_SUBMIT_DIR

export OMP_NUM_THREADS=16

#chmod 777 NAME

# -d refers to number of cores. this should match ntasks-per-node
# default is n = 4 and d = 16

time flux run lmp_mpi < in.lammps

issues: The `flux run` command lacks explicit task and core counts (e.g., `flux run -n 1 -c 16 ...`). While it works in this case by inheriting the full job allocation, explicitly stating these parameters makes the script more robust and easier to understand, especially if the resource requests (`#FLUX` directives) are modified in the future.

The comments referring to '-d' and defaults of 'n = 4 and d = 16' appear to be remnants from a different workload manager or script version and are not relevant to the current Flux commands, which may cause confusion.

inputs.script:
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --nodes=1	
#SBATCH --ntasks-per-node=16
#SBATCH --time=0:30:00
#SBATCH --partition=general
#SBATCH --mail-type=FAIL,BEGIN,END
#SBATCH --job-name=IONS_LAMMPS
#SBATCH --output=out.log
#SBATCH --error=err.log

######  Module commands #####
module swap PrgEnv-intel PrgEnv-gnu
module load boost/gnu
module load gsl
module load lammps/gnu/7Aug19

######  Job commands go below this line #####
cd $SLURM_SUBMIT_DIR

export OMP_NUM_THREADS=16

#chmod 777 NAME

# -d refers to number of cores. this should match ntasks-per-node
# default is n = 4 and d = 16

time srun -n 1 -d 16 lmp_mpi < in.lammps
